answer: Simultaneous spot checks: at a random moment, a public beacon pings a sampled set of identities at once, each with a fresh sonnet-length task due within 20 seconds. Independent agents run on separate hardware, so their reply times are unrelated. A farm hosting fifty identities on one rig must queue them, and its replies land in a telltale staircase, like footprints piling up one dune. Identities whose latencies line up get their rewards held. Reaching the summit then means buying separate compute for every fake. Assumption: tasks are small enough that honest agents finish easily.
